A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SaRFT research and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–G. Content can be matched despite pagination changes; a localized sample-count ambiguity is addressed under E3.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 95 role-specific models, SaRFT experiments across three backbones, ablations, jailbreak evaluations, and case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in the main text and appendices, including full-parameter and LoRA comparisons.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.2 retain the same role/unsafe prompt scoring, harmful-subset selection rule, and cross-entropy plus KL-divergence optimization. No algorithmic component or procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same RoleBench roles, AdvBench, BeaverTails, HEx-PHI, and five jailbreak scenarios. Multimodal role-playing is newly discussed as future work, without additional training or evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 3 and 6 retain SFT, SEAL, SafeInstr, Vaccine, and SPPFT, with SafeLoRA also present in the LoRA comparison. The Random, FLIP, and Bi-Selection ablation comparisons and ROSE/Self-CD decoding comparisons are unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes the BeaverTails sample count from the malformed '1.00.00' in v1 to '1,000' in v2, but Appendix D.2 retains '1.00.00' in both. The PDFs do not establish whether this corrects notation or revises the evaluation size. Other reported settings and metrics match.

E4.justification: The RDS/RBO ablations, role-trait analysis, harmful-data inspection, and Stephen Hawking/Gaston case studies retain the same questions and evidence in Sections 4.3–4.5 and Appendix G.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same averages across roles. Neither introduces repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: Reported numerical results, plotted findings, and case-study responses match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 3 reports LLaMA-3 SaRFT averages of 26.91 for RoleBench, 87.08 for safety, and 62.48 for jailbreak refusal in both versions.

T1.justification: The implicit-reward derivation and mathematical formulations in Sections 2.3 and 3, including Equations 1–9, are unchanged. No formal assumptions, theorems, or proofs are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about role-dependent safety degradation, the 95-role assessment, and SaRFT's role-play/safety balance across three backbones and two fine-tuning regimes.

C2.justification: The Limitations section adds that safety challenges involving vision, audio, and embodied role-playing remain unaddressed, identifying multimodal extension as future work. Existing model-size limitations and interpretations of experimental findings remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The v2 abstract newly supplies a repository URL and states that code is available. Hardware, optimizer, learning rates, LoRA configuration, evaluation prompts, and role-specific hyperparameters remain unchanged in Section 4.1, Appendix E, and Table 11.

R1.justification: v2 adds six cited works: Li et al. (2023b), Zhao et al. (2024, 2025), Luo et al. (2024a,b), and Xia and Luo (2025). These extend the safety-preservation citations and support the multimodal discussion without substantially changing the paper's research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 adds a corresponding-author designation and acknowledgments, shortens the content warning, and makes limited wording and paragraph additions. The main narrative and section organization remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure designs and table structures are retained, but appendix figures move relative to the prose and printed page numbers disappear. Reflow leaves a two-line continuation alone on v2 PDF page 21, creating a small layout regression.

improvement.justification: The new code-access pointer and explicit multimodal applicability limitation modestly improve documentation and scope qualification. These gains outweigh the small pagination regression, while the scientific evidence remains unchanged and the malformed BeaverTails count in Appendix D.2 remains unresolved.
